title: Selected Topics in Aerospace Engineering; Hydrodynamic Stability II
description:
Prerequisite: ENAR788Q or permission of instructor.

This course will provide students with an overview of hydrodynamic stability for compressible and three-dimensional boundary layer flows. Both inviscid and viscous instability mechanisms will be explored as well as the effects of wall cooling and heating on the boundary layer stability. Additional considerations relevant for 3D boundary layers will also be considered. Key concepts such as parallel flow stability equations, normal mode equations, the effect of Mach number on viscous instability, receptivity in high-speed wind tunnels, streamwise instability, and crossflow instability will be covered. Various instability problems will be investigated such as rotating disk boundary layers, Falker-Skan-Cooke boundary layers and transonic infinite-span swept-wingboundary layers.
